root_cause.text: In `ovs_netdev_tunnel_destroy()`, the RCU callback `call_rcu(&vport->rcu, vport_netdev_free)` that releases the netdev reference was placed after `rtnl_unlock()`, but `rtnl_unlock()` triggers `netdev_run_todo()` which blocks until all netdev references are released, causing a self-deadlock because the callback is never invoked.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `call_rcu()` before `rtnl_unlock()`. The commit message explains: "when the device is deleted, rtnl_unlock() will call netdev_run_todo() and block until all the references are gone. In the current code this means that we never reach the call_rcu() and the vport is never freed and the reference is never released, causing a self-deadlock on device removal."
